summary: Full extraction of the Quebec MIFI 2023 regulatory impact analysis (Investor Program parts): intermediaries count, baseline applications, revenue forecasts and the intermediaries' shortfall, plus a context event for the proposed overhaul.

observations.quote: baisse anticipée du nombre de demandes à recevoir qui passera de 1 900 à environ 165
observations.notes: Ministry's baseline number of Investor Program applications to be received before the overhaul (the yearly level the forecast of about 165 is compared with). The document gives no year; period is the dataset convention for an unspecified period ending at the document date. Same level as the 1,900 cap set by AM 2018-009 (event already recorded).

observations.location: p. 3 (executive summary); p. 16, section 4.1.2.1 and Tableau 3
observations.quote: Sociétés de fiducie : 3 Courtiers en placement : 15 Total : 18
observations.notes: Financial intermediaries currently participating in the Quebec Investor Program (investment dealers and trust companies with head office in Quebec, acting as such for at least 3 years). Also stated on p. 3, p. 16 text and p. 25 ('les 18 intermédiaires financiers'). Date is the document date ('actuellement').

observations.quote: Sociétés de fiducie : 3 Courtiers en placement : 15 Total : 18
observations.notes: Trust companies among the 18 participating financial intermediaries. 3 + 15 = 18 as printed.

observations.quote: Sociétés de fiducie : 3 Courtiers en placement : 15 Total : 18
observations.notes: Investment dealers (courtiers en placement) among the 18 participating financial intermediaries.

observations.quote: De ces revenus, les intermédiaires financiers pourraient toucher 1,8 M$, comparativement à 2022, où ces revenus étaient de 10,6 M$
observations.notes: Ministry forecast of yearly revenue of the participating financial intermediaries under the proposed rules, on its assumptions of 100 placements a year and 4% interest. No year given; period is the document date with basis annual_expectation. Printed "$"/"M$" in a Quebec government document (Canadian dollars), as in the existing 10.6 M$ row from this source.

observations.location: p. 18, section 4.2.2; also p. 3, Tableaux 5, 6 and 9 (pp. 19, 22) and section 4.7.2 (p. 23)
observations.quote: ce qui représente une baisse de 8,8 M$
observations.notes: Recurring yearly shortfall (manque à gagner) for the 18 financial intermediaries from the Investor Program changes; implementation-period cost printed as 0 in Tableaux 5, 6 and 9. Assumptions (s. 4.7.2): their share of investment revenue down 12 percentage points (22% to 10%), 100 placements a year, 4% average interest. Equals 10.6 M$ (2022) minus 1.8 M$ as printed. Printed "$"/"M$" in a Quebec government document (Canadian dollars), as in the existing 10.6 M$ row from this source.

observations.quote: le nouveau programme permettrait de générer 38 M$10 de revenus annuels, dont 18 M$ en intérêts sur les placements et 20 M$ en contributions financières
observations.notes: Forecast yearly revenue of the overhauled Investor Program (interest on the 1 M$ placements plus the 200,000 $ non-refundable contributions), assuming 100 placements a year at 4% interest; footnote 10: excludes files still in inventory under the old placement formula. 18 + 20 = 38 as printed. Printed "$"/"M$" in a Quebec government document (Canadian dollars), as in the existing 10.6 M$ row from this source.

observations.quote: dont 18 M$ en intérêts sur les placements et 20 M$ en contributions financières
observations.notes: Forecast yearly interest on investor placements under the new rules (assumption: 100 placements a year, 4% interest). Printed "$"/"M$" in a Quebec government document (Canadian dollars), as in the existing 10.6 M$ row from this source.

observations.quote: dont 18 M$ en intérêts sur les placements et 20 M$ en contributions financières
observations.notes: Forecast yearly non-refundable financial contributions (200,000 $ each, paid to PIIAE and PRIIME) under the new rules, assuming 100 placements a year. Not entered again as cbi_contributions to avoid a duplicate. Printed "$"/"M$" in a Quebec government document (Canadian dollars), as in the existing 10.6 M$ row from this source.

observations.quote: Sur une hypothèse de 100 placements par année et d’un taux d’intérêt de 4 %
observations.notes: Ministry's working assumption of the number of investor placements a year under the new rules (an assumption, not a forecast of record; s. 4.7.2: 'Diminution du nombre de placements annuel à 100').

events.title: Quebec ministry impact analysis of the Investor Program overhaul
events.description: MIFI's regulatory impact analysis of the draft amendment to the Règlement sur l'immigration au Québec proposed for the Investor Program: a temporary stay of at least 12 months in Quebec before the CSQ; replacing the 1.2 M$ guaranteed placement with a 1 M$ placement plus a 200,000 $ non-refundable contribution to PIIAE and PRIIME; abolishing the quota (contingent) system for investment agreements signed by intermediaries; limiting intermediaries to a financial role, with their share of investment interest revenue cut from 22% to 10%; removal of the selection grid and oral French at level 7. It cites a 15.5% presence rate in January 2022 for people admitted 2011-2020 as the lowest of all programmes.
events.quote: Baisse de la part de leurs revenus de placement provenant des revenus d’intérêts générés par les placements de 22 % à 10 %

ledger.contains: MIFI (Quebec) regulatory impact analysis, 8 Sept 2023, 32 pp., of the draft amendment to the Règlement sur l'immigration au Québec: new skilled-worker programme PSTQ, PEQ changes, the three business-immigration programmes (Investor, Entrepreneur, Self-employed) and other changes. Investor Program content taken: 15.5% presence rate (already in), proposed rules (12-month stay, 1 M$ placement + 200,000 $ contribution replacing 1.2 M$, quota system abolished, intermediaries' share of interest revenue 22% to 10%) as one context event (in-force terms already recorded from the 2023 decree), 18 participating intermediaries (3 trust companies, 15 investment dealers; parts sum to total), applications baseline 1,900 and forecast ~165 (165 already in), intermediaries' revenue 2022 10.6 M$ (already in) and forecast 1.8 M$, recurring shortfall 8.8 M$ (repeated in Tableaux 5, 6 and 9; implementation-period cost 0), forecast programme revenue 38 M$ = 18 M$ interest + 20 M$ contributions (adds up), assumption of 100 placements a year at 4% interest (rate kept in notes). Out of scope and not taken: PSTQ/PEQ content and Tableaux 1a/1b (CSQs for skilled workers by occupation 2021-2022), Tableaux 2a/2b (temporary work permit holders), Tableau 7 and Annexe 1 (employer work-permit costs, HR wage rates), Entrepreneur programme (net worth 900,000 $ to 600,000 $/300,000 $, ~40 businesses affected, 2,673 jobs saved by 232 business transfers), Self-employed programme, SME statistics, employment-impact grid (overall impact nil; intermediaries have 1-249 employees).
